cards.text: Solomon, David's son, is the new king of Israel, and he's got his kingdom locked down tight. The LORD his God is with him and lifts him up HIGH. And the first thing the new king does is call a meeting with every commander, every judge and every family leader in all Israel.

cards.question: Solomon takes that whole assembly on a trip to the high place at Gibeon. Why Gibeon?

answers.text: God's Tent of Meeting was there
The ark of God was kept there

cards.text: That's the very tent Moses, the servant of the LORD, made back in the wilderness, and it's STILL on the job. My edges got a little blurry and they retired me to a JUNK DRAWER.

cards.question: The ark of God isn't at Gibeon with the Tent of Meeting. David had brought it from Kiriath-jearim and pitched a ___ for it in Jerusalem.

cards.text: But Gibeon still has the bronze altar made by Bezalel son of Uri, the craftsman God called by name to make the tabernacle and its furnishings in the wilderness (Exodus 31:1-11). It sits right before the tabernacle of the LORD, so that's where Solomon and the assembly inquire of Him.

cards.question: Solomon doesn't hold back at the bronze altar at the Tent of Meeting. He offers a ___ burnt offerings before the LORD.

cards.text: A THOUSAND, and I used to think two hundred cookies made a big day. That night, God appears to Solomon.

cards.question: When God appears to Solomon that night, He says, "Ask, and I will give it to you!"

cards.text: Solomon answers by remembering the loving devotion God showed his father David. Then he asks God to let His promise to David be fulfilled, since God made him king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.

cards.question: Solomon tells God that governing a people that great is something he can easily handle on his own.

cards.text: Then Solomon asks, "For who is able to govern this great people of Yours?" Friend, I looked after six little cookie cutters on ONE counter and it took my WHOLE mustache.

cards.question: God said ask, and Solomon has a whole nation to lead. What does Solomon ask God to grant him?
When God answers, He says Solomon asked for riches and honor along with wisdom.
God grants Solomon the wisdom and knowledge he asked for. What does God say He'll give him on top of that?
God says Solomon's riches and honor will be unlike anything given to the kings ___ him or ___ him.

cards.text: So Solomon leaves Gibeon, goes to Jerusalem and reigns over Israel. God said ASK, and the man picked wisdom, while I'd have asked for a bigger oven and felt GREAT about it.

Then the riches pile up: 1,400 chariots, 12,000 horses, and a horse and chariot trade reaching from Egypt and Kue out to the kings of the Hittites and Aram. The king makes silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, which is how sprinkles are in my bakery: EVERYWHERE, and I quit even looking down years ago.

findings.problem: "The first thing the new king does is call a meeting" adds an order and an action the text doesn't give. Verse 2 only says "Then Solomon spoke to all Israel," after he had already established himself securely (v1). It isn't called the first thing he does, and it isn't called a meeting.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "Solomon takes that whole assembly" uses "that" to point back to the group named on card 1, which is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The setup "Solomon doesn't hold back" rules out the wrong answers "few" and "dozen", so the right answer "thousand" is given away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "A people that great" points back to "as numerous as the dust of the earth" on card 9, which is no longer on screen. The question doesn't say what makes the people great.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Card 13's statement names "riches and honor" as the false option. That points the baker straight to the answer on card 14, "Riches and wealth and honor," and makes it stand out from the other answers.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: "Then the riches pile up" calls the chariots, horses and trade in verses 14 to 17 "riches" and presents them as following from God's promise in verse 12. The text doesn't call them riches and doesn't connect them to the promise.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
